questions.question: Elaborate upon Sexual Dimorphism in Fishes?
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the sexual dimorphism between male and female Amia calva
  • Male
  • Possesses a distinct black spot (ocellus) at the base of the caudal (tail) fin, usually
  • surrounded by an orange or yellow ring.
  • Body may appear slightly more slender.
  • During breeding season, males guard the nest and eggs.
  • Female
  • Lacks the prominent black spot at the base of the caudal fin
  • Generally broader or fuller body, especially when carrying eggs.
  • Does not exhibit nest-guarding behavior.
  • Sex is fixed by sex chromosomes or specific genes inherited from parents.
  • It is similar to mechanisms seen in ot her animals, where combinations like
  • XX/XY or ZZ/ZW determine sex.
  • Once determined, the sex generally does not change due to environmental factors
  • (though some exceptions exist in fishes).
  • Examples
  • XX/XY system
  • XX → Female
  • XY → Male
  • ZZ/ZW system
  • ZZ → Male
  • ZW → Female
  • Leads to a lighter body colour
  • Pigment Dispersing Hormone (PDH)
  • Results in a darker body colour
  • Helps in light and dark adaptation of vision
  • Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone analogues (GnRHa), SGnRHa
  • Phenoxyethanol : No buffering needed, Stable in water
  • Clove oil (Eugenol) : Natural, low cost, Common in hatcheries
  • Quinaldine : Used in marine fishes
  • Importance / Uses: Reduces stress during handling, Prevents injury to fish & handler
  • Facilitates breeding operations
  • Stripping of eggs & milt , Artificial fertilization
  • Ease of transport , Accurate measurements (length, weight) , Tagging, surgery
  • sampling, Improves survival rate, Minimizes metabolic activity
  • Methods of administration
  • Immersion (most common) : Fish placed in anaesthetic solution , Absorption
  • through gills
  • Dip method : High concentration, short duration
  • Prolonged bath : Low concentration, long exposure
  • Irrigation method : Anaesthetic water passed over gills, Used during surgery
  • Stages of anaesthesia
  • Light sedation → loss of equilibrium → deep anaesthesia → recovery
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: Light sedation → loss of equilibrium → deep anaesthesia → recovery
